reasons: Deviation is real: original p0088 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work 'including any Improvements or Modifications thereto', which captures the bespoke Schedule 'D' Modifications the Customer commissions and pays for, and the Section 2 licence covers only Software/Documentation, so there is no clear licence back — squarely within the rule's 'Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back' trigger.

Redline reaches the preferred position: it removes 'Modifications' from Garman's blanket ownership parenthetical, adds an assignment to Sparkling of the Modifications and other customer-funded deliverables, carves out Garman pre-existing/independently developed IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back for embedded Vendor IP, confirms Customer retains all rights in its data and converted/processed data, and expressly negates joint ownership.

Vendor's ownership of its own platform/Work and related materials, logos and names is preserved, and the 'Except as expressly set out in this Section 13' qualifier resolves the conflict with the no-transfer sentence, so the edit is internally coherent and no broader than the rule requires.

Failed 'minimal edit' check (0.767 changed-character ratio) is advisory only here: the added assignment, licence-back, Customer Data and no-joint-ownership sentences are all mandated by the rule's redline guidance and cannot be achieved with a shorter edit; the original text is otherwise left intact.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, correctly states the playbook position ('we own what we pay for and everything we put in') and offers the sanctioned fallback (Vendor ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
